cover: RAG and fine-tuning, in plain terms

slides.title: The model doesn't know your documents
slides.body: It learned from public text up to a cutoff date. Your policies, manuals and contracts were never part of that.

slides.title: RAG looks things up
slides.body: The system searches your documents for relevant passages and hands them to the model along with the question.

slides.title: Like an open-book exam
slides.body: The model writes the answer, the facts come from your documents, and you can check the passage it used.

slides.title: Fine-tuning changes the model
slides.body: Training on hundreds of agreed examples builds in a format or tone, so it no longer needs long instructions.

slides.title: A poor place to keep facts
slides.body: A tuned model keeps what it learned at training time and can't show where an answer came from.

slides.title: Try a better prompt first
slides.body: Clear instructions and a few good examples are often enough, and they give you a baseline to measure against.
